artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

perplexity.description:
The Very Very Best Of Crowded House, released in 2010 by Universal Music, is a career-spanning compilation that showcases the band’s signature blend of melodic rock, jangly guitar textures, and heartfelt songwriting. The album features 19 tracks drawn from Crowded House’s most celebrated periods, including hits like “Don’t Dream It’s Over,” “Weather With You,” and “Better Be Home Soon.” Musically, the collection highlights the group’s knack for crafting accessible yet emotionally resonant pop-rock, anchored by Neil Finn’s distinctive vocals and lyrical introspection, as well as the band’s rich harmonies and dynamic arrangements.

This compilation serves as a definitive overview of Crowded House’s legacy, bridging their 1986 self-titled debut through their 2007 reunion album Time On Earth. It captures the evolution of their sound—from the straightforward pop of their early years to the more textured, experimental work of their later albums. Upon its original release, The Very Very Best Of Crowded House was a commercial success, reaching the Top 20 in both Australia and New Zealand and earning widespread acclaim for its thoughtful track selection and enduring appeal. The album stands as a testament to the band’s lasting influence in the rock genre and remains a go-to introduction for new listeners and a cherished collection for longtime fans.
